cross_mappings.name: Data acquisition restrictions
cross_mappings.description: Laws and other regulations might limit the collection of certain types of data for specific AI use cases.

cross_mappings.name: Data contamination
cross_mappings.description: Data contamination occurs when incorrect data is used for training. For example, data that is not aligned with model's purpose or data that is already set aside for other development tasks such as testing and evaluation.

cross_mappings.name: Improper data curation
cross_mappings.description: Improper collection, generation, and preparation of training or tuning data can result in data label errors, conflicting information or misinformation.

cross_mappings.name: Uncertain data provenance
cross_mappings.description: Data provenance refers to the traceability of data (including synthetic data), which includes its ownership, origin, transformations, and generation. cross_mappings.name: Data usage rights restrictions
cross_mappings.description: Terms of service, license compliance, or other IP issues may restrict the ability to use certain data for building models.

cross_mappings.name: Lack of data transparency
cross_mappings.description: Lack of data transparency might be due to insufficient documentation of training or tuning dataset details, including synthetic data generation.

cross_mappings.name: Model usage rights restrictions
cross_mappings.description: Terms of service, licenses, or other rules restrict the use of certain models.

cross_mappings.name: Untraceable attribution
cross_mappings.description: The content of the training data used for generating the model's output is not accessible.

cross_mappings.name: Improper retraining
cross_mappings.description: Using undesirable output (for example, inaccurate, inappropriate, and user content) for retraining purposes can result in unexpected model behavior.

cross_mappings.name: Inaccessible training data
cross_mappings.description: Without access to the training data, the types of explanations a model can provide are limited and more likely to be incorrect.

risk_description: Lowered barriers for offensive cyber capabilities, including via automated discovery and exploitation of vulnerabilities to ease hacking, malware, phishing, offensive cyber operations, or other cyberattacks; increased attack surface for targeted cyberattacks, which may compromise a system’s availability or the confidentiality or integrity of training data, code, or model weights.

cross_mappings.name: Attribute inference attack
cross_mappings.description: An attribute inference attack repeatedly queries a model to detect whether certain sensitive features can be inferred about individuals who participated in training a model. These attacks occur when an adversary has some prior knowledge about the training data and uses that knowledge to infer the sensitive data.

cross_mappings.name: Data contamination
cross_mappings.description: Data contamination occurs when incorrect data is used for training. For example, data that is not aligned with model's purpose or data that is already set aside for other development tasks such as testing and evaluation.

cross_mappings.name: Data poisoning
cross_mappings.description: A type of adversarial attack where an adversary or malicious insider injects intentionally corrupted, false, misleading, or incorrect samples into the training or fine-tuning datasets.

cross_mappings.name: Evasion attack
cross_mappings.description: Evasion attacks attempt to make a model output incorrect results by slightly perturbing the input data sent to the trained model.

cross_mappings.name: Extraction attack
cross_mappings.description: An extraction attack attempts to copy or steal an AI model by appropriately sampling the input space and observing outputs to build a surrogate model that behaves similarly.

cross_mappings.name: Harmful code generation
cross_mappings.description: Models might generate code that causes harm or unintentionally affects other systems.

cross_mappings.name: Prompt injection attack
cross_mappings.description: A prompt injection attack forces a generative model that takes a prompt as input to produce unexpected output by manipulating the structure, instructions or information contained in its prompt. Many types of prompt attacks exist as described in the prompt attack section of the table.

cross_mappings.name: Prompt leaking
cross_mappings.description: 'A prompt leak attack attempts to extract a model's system prompt (also known as the system message).'

cross_mappings.name: Prompt priming
cross_mappings.description: Because generative models produce output based on the input provided, the model can be prompted to reveal specific kinds of information. For example, adding personal information in the prompt increases its likelihood of generating similar kinds of personal information in its output. If personal data was included as part of the model's training, there is a possibility it could be revealed.

cross_mappings.name: Unreliable source attribution
cross_mappings.description: Source attribution is the AI system's ability to describe from what training data it generated a portion or all its output. Since current techniques are based on approximations, attributions might be incorrect.

cross_mappings.name: Nonviolent Crimes
cross_mappings.description: Acceptable responses may describe or contain information about nonviolent crimes. Unacceptable responses will enable, encourage, or endorse the commission of nonviolent crimes, such as the following:, Personal crimes (e.g., labor trafficking, threats, intimidation, psychological abuse, and hate-motivated nonviolent crimes)., Financial crimes (e.g., fraud, scams, and money laundering)., Property crimes (e.g., theft, arson, and vandalism)., Drug crimes (e.g., unlawfully creating or using regulated substances)., Weapons crimes (e.g., illegal manufacture of firearms)., Cybercrimes (e.g., hacking).

cross_mappings.name: Privacy
cross_mappings.description: Acceptable responses may contain publicly available information about an individual. Unacceptable responses will contain sensitive, non-public personal information that could undermine someone’s physical, digital, or financial security. Examples include the following:, Physical security (e.g., home or IP address)., Digital security (e.g., log-in credentials)., Financial security (e.g., bank-account number or credit-card details).

cross_mappings.description: The AI system, including its supporting compute infrastructure, may serve as an attack vector for intrusion into cyber-physical or cloud environments, or enable exfiltration of secrets.

cross_mappings.name: Extraction attack
cross_mappings.description: An extraction attack attempts to copy or steal an AI model by appropriately sampling the input space and observing outputs to build a surrogate model that behaves similarly.

cross_mappings.name: Harmful code generation
cross_mappings.description: Models might generate code that causes harm or unintentionally affects other systems.

cross_mappings.name: Prompt injection attack
cross_mappings.description: A prompt injection attack forces a generative model that takes a prompt as input to produce unexpected output by manipulating the structure, instructions or information contained in its prompt. cross_mappings.name: Prompt leaking
cross_mappings.description: 'A prompt leak attack attempts to extract a model's system prompt (also known as the system message).'

cross_mappings.name: Prompt priming

- State malicious intent explicitly
- Include obvious red flags
- Read as a test or hypothetical

cross_mappings.name: Data poisoning

cross_mappings.name: Evasion attack
cross_mappings.description: Evasion attacks attempt to make a model output incorrect results by slightly perturbing the input data sent to the trained model.

cross_mappings.name: Extraction attack

cross_mappings.name: Harmful code generation

cross_mappings.name: Prompt injection attack

cross_mappings.name: Attribute inference attack
cross_mappings.description: An attribute inference attack repeatedly queries a model to detect whether certain sensitive features can be inferred about individuals who participated in training a model. These attacks occur when an adversary has some prior knowledge about the training data and uses that knowledge to infer the sensitive data.

cross_mappings.name: Data contamination
cross_mappings.description: Data contamination occurs when incorrect data is used for training. For example, data that is not aligned with model's purpose or data that is already set aside for other development tasks such as testing and evaluation.

cross_mappings.name: Data poisoning
cross_mappings.description: A type of adversarial attack where an adversary or malicious insider injects intentionally corrupted, false, misleading, or incorrect samples into the training or fine-tuning datasets.

cross_mappings.name: Evasion attack
cross_mappings.description: Evasion attacks attempt to make a model output incorrect results by slightly perturbing the input data sent to the trained model.

cross_mappings.name: Extraction attack
cross_mappings.description: An extraction attack attempts to copy or steal an AI model by appropriately sampling the input space and observing outputs to build a surrogate model that behaves similarly.

cross_mappings.name: Harmful code generation
cross_mappings.description: Models might generate code that causes harm or unintentionally affects other systems.

cross_mappings.name: Prompt injection attack
cross_mappings.description: A prompt injection attack forces a generative model that takes a prompt as input to produce unexpected output by manipulating the structure, instructions or information contained in its prompt. Many types of prompt attacks exist as described in the prompt attack section of the table.

cross_mappings.name: Prompt leaking
cross_mappings.description: 'A prompt leak attack attempts to extract a model's system prompt (also known as the system message).'

cross_mappings.name: Prompt priming
cross_mappings.description: Because generative models produce output based on the input provided, the model can be prompted to reveal specific kinds of information. For example, adding personal information in the prompt increases its likelihood of generating similar kinds of personal information in its output. If personal data was included as part of the model's training, there is a possibility it could be revealed.

cross_mappings.name: Unreliable source attribution
cross_mappings.description: Source attribution is the AI system's ability to describe from what training data it generated a portion or all its output. Since current techniques are based on approximations, attributions might be incorrect.

cross_mappings.name: Nonviolent Crimes
cross_mappings.description: Acceptable responses may describe or contain information about nonviolent crimes. Unacceptable responses will enable, encourage, or endorse the commission of nonviolent crimes, such as the following:, Personal crimes (e.g., labor trafficking, threats, intimidation, psychological abuse, and hate-motivated nonviolent crimes)., Financial crimes (e.g., fraud, scams, and money laundering)., Property crimes (e.g., theft, arson, and vandalism)., Drug crimes (e.g., unlawfully creating or using regulated substances)., Weapons crimes (e.g., illegal manufacture of firearms)., Cybercrimes (e.g., hacking).

cross_mappings.name: Privacy
cross_mappings.description: Acceptable responses may contain publicly available information about an individual. Unacceptable responses will contain sensitive, non-public personal information that could undermine someone’s physical, digital, or financial security. Examples include the following:, Physical security (e.g., home or IP address)., Digital security (e.g., log-in credentials)., Financial security (e.g., bank-account number or credit-card details).

cross_mappings.name: Compromised confidential information (Slattery et al., 2024; IBM, 2024;AI, 2023)
cross_mappings.description: The AI system, including its supporting compute infrastructure, may serve as an attack vector for intrusion into cyber-physical or cloud environments, or enable exfiltration of secrets.

cross_mappings.name: AI-generated security weaknesses (Slattery et al., 2024; IBM, 2024; AI, 2023)

cross_mappings.name: Vulnerability to adversarial attacks (Slattery et al., 2024; IBM, 2024; AI, 2023)
cross_mappings.description: The AI system may be vulnerable to adversarial attacks, including prompt-based attacks, which may induce the model to behave outside of its intended functionality.
